# Maine Wild Food Survival Guide

## First Principles
- Never eat anything you can't identify with certainty. Learn a few species well rather than many poorly.
- Boil all water. Beaver ponds and slow streams carry giardia.
- Calories matter more than vitamins in the first weeks. Fat and starch keep you alive; greens only supplement.
- Eat nothing raw from animals. Cook thoroughly.

## Spring (April to June)
- **Fiddleheads (ostrich fern):** Tightly coiled, with a smooth stem and a deep U-shaped groove on the inside. Found along river banks. Boil 10 to 15 minutes, discard the water. Never eat them raw.
- **Wild leeks (ramps):** Broad leaves in rich hardwood forests. Eat bulbs and leaves.
- **Cattail:** Roots, shoots and young flower spikes in marshes. The roots can be pounded in water to release starch.
- **Dandelion, wood sorrel, chickweed:** Common greens. Eat sorrel in moderation.
- **Birch and maple sap:** Drink it or boil it down. Sugar maple syrup needs roughly forty parts sap to one.

## Summer (June to August)
- **Wild strawberries, raspberries, blackberries:** Roadsides, clearings and old fields.
- **Lowbush blueberries:** Abundant on coastal barrens and mountain ledges. Dry them in the sun to store.
- **Chanterelles:** Orange-gold, with false gills that run down the stem and a fruity smell. Under conifers and hardwoods after rain.
- **Fish:** Brook trout, landlocked salmon, perch and pickerel. Make a hook from a bent thorn, or build a stone weir in a shallow stream.

## Autumn (September to November)
- **Acorns:** Red oak acorns are bitter. Crack them, then soak or boil in several changes of water until the water runs clear. Grind into flour.
- **Beechnuts, hickory nuts, butternuts:** High in fat. Collect as many as you can.
- **Cranberries and rosehips:** Cranberries grow in bogs, and rosehips are rich in vitamin C. Both last into winter.
- **Hen-of-the-woods and puffballs:** Hen-of-the-woods grows in clusters at the base of oaks. Eat only puffballs that are pure white and solid inside. Cut each one open to check.
- **Deer, moose, rabbit, snowshoe hare, grouse, porcupine:** Snares and deadfalls are more reliable than chasing. Porcupines are slow and have long been a traditional emergency food.

## Winter
- **Pine, spruce and hemlock needles:** Steep them for a vitamin C tea. Avoid yew, which is toxic.
- **Inner bark (cambium) of white pine:** Last-resort starvation food.
- **Ice fishing:** Lakes freeze thick enough for chopping a hole. Fish are easier to catch in cold water.
- **Cached nuts and dried berries:** Preserve in autumn, because winter foraging is poor.

## Coast
- **Clams, mussels, periwinkles:** Harvest from clean tidal flats at low tide. Avoid shellfish in summer, when red tide can occur. If the water is discolored or the shellfish seem to be dying off, skip them.
- **Seaweed:** Dulse, kelp and sea lettuce. Rinse, dry and eat.
- **Lobster:** Boil or roast. Traps built from sticks work in shallow water.

## Deadly Look-Alikes
- **Water hemlock** resembles wild carrot and is among the most poisonous plants in North America.
- **Amanita mushrooms** (destroying angel, death cap) have white gills and a cup at the base.
- **Baneberry and pokeweed berries** are toxic.
- Do not eat white or red berries you cannot name.

## Fire, Water and Shelter
Calories burned keeping warm count as much as calories eaten, so a lean-to against a rock face with a reflector fire is worth the effort. Maine winters can drop well below zero, and without shelter and fire, food will not save you.

Space Exploration or Problems on Earth?

Many people ask if governments should spend money on space exploration. Some people think this money should be used to solve problems on Earth, like hunger, sickness and poverty. I think both sides have good points, but I believe governments should spend a small part of their money on space, and most of it on problems here.

First, I understand why people are against space spending. Every day, many people in the world do not have enough food or clean water. Hospitals in poor countries often does not have enough doctors or medicine. When I see this, it is hard to say that sending a rocket to Mars is more important. Rockets are very expensive, and one launch can cost hundreds of millions of dollars. This money could build many schools or clinics.

However, space exploration also gives us many benefits. For example, scientists who work on space projects invented many things we use every day. Satellites give us weather information, so farmers can know when it will rain and people can get ready for big storms. GPS in our phones also comes from space technology. Some medical tools were also developed from research for astronauts. So the money is not really lost in the sky. It comes back to Earth in another form.

Also, space research can teach us about our own planet. By looking at Earth from space, scientists can see how the climate is changing and how forests are getting smaller. This information help governments make better decisions. In the future, space may even give us new resources or a new place to live if Earth has big problems.

Another point is that space projects give many people jobs. Engineers, scientists, builders and teachers all work on them. Young people become interested in science because they dream about being astronauts. This is good for the future of a country.

Still, I think governments must be careful. The space budget is usually only a small part of all government spending, so it is not the main reason why problems on Earth are not solved. But if a country has many people without homes or food, solving those problems should come first. A good government should look after its people before it looks at the stars.

In conclusion, I think space exploration is useful and we should not stop it completely. But governments should spend most of their money on problems on Earth, and keep space spending small and smart. In this way, we can take care of today and also prepare for tomorrow.

# Adrian Peterson Must Continue Counseling as Part of Suspension, Goodell Says

NEW YORK — Minnesota Vikings running back Adrian Peterson will be required to continue counseling and other treatment as a condition of his return to the NFL, Commissioner Roger Goodell said, following Peterson's suspension and guilty plea in a child abuse case.

Peterson, who had been suspended by the league, pleaded guilty to misdemeanor reckless assault. Goodell has made clear that the running back's reinstatement depends on his willingness to follow a program of counseling and treatment. The commissioner's requirements mean Peterson cannot simply return to the field once his suspension ends. He must also show that he is taking steps to address the conduct that led to the charge.

The league has said little about the details of the treatment program, including how long it will last or how his progress will be measured. Such conditions are not unusual in NFL disciplinary cases. The league has increasingly tied reinstatement to participation in counseling and similar programs, particularly in cases involving violence away from the field.

The Vikings, who finished 7-9 last season, said they look forward to having Peterson rejoin the team. The club has a clear on-field interest in his return. Peterson has been one of the most productive running backs in the league, and the team's offense struggled to find consistency without him. In a statement, the franchise said it supports the process and hopes to welcome him back once he meets the league's conditions.

Peterson's case drew widespread attention and sharp debate over how professional sports leagues handle discipline for off-field conduct, particularly when children are involved. Critics said the league had been slow to respond to abuse allegations involving its players. Supporters of Peterson said he should be allowed to return to work after accepting responsibility in court and serving his suspension.

Neither Peterson nor his representatives were immediately available for comment on the league's requirements. It remains unclear when he could be formally reinstated, as the league has not announced a timeline.

For now, the focus shifts to whether Peterson will meet the conditions Goodell has laid out, and whether the Vikings, coming off a losing season, can rebuild with him back in the lineup.

text: **Abstract.** Organic traffic is a primary source of customer acquisition for e-commerce platforms, and its volume depends heavily on how product feeds are presented to search engines and discovery surfaces. In practice, merchants optimize titles, descriptions, and attributes by hand or with fixed heuristics, which scale poorly and adapt slowly to changes in ranking behavior. We formulate the optimization of product feed content as a sequential decision problem and propose a reinforcement learning framework that learns to generate and select feed modifications in order to maximize expected organic traffic. The framework relies on a learned traffic estimator, trained on historical impression and click data, to provide reward signals without requiring costly live experimentation for every candidate edit. To address the sparsity and delay of organic feedback, we introduce a counterfactual correction that reduces bias in the estimated rewards, together with a constrained action space that preserves factual accuracy and compliance with platform policies. Experiments on a large-scale offline dataset drawn from an operating e-commerce marketplace show consistent gains in predicted clicks over rule-based and supervised baselines. A subsequent online A/B test confirms a statistically significant increase in organic visits without any degradation in conversion rate. These results indicate that learning-based feed optimization is a practical and effective strategy for increasing organic reach.

text:
The Last Thing I Remembered

It happened on a Tuesday, which seemed unfair. Gods deserve better days than Tuesdays.

I was standing in the checkout line at a grocery store in Fresno, holding a carton of eggs and a coupon for laundry detergent, when the knowledge arrived. It did not feel like a thought. It felt like remembering my own phone number. Oh, right. I am God. The stars, the platypus, the particular shade of orange on the fruit stand across the aisle, all of it came from me. I had simply stepped away for a while.

The woman in front of me was arguing with the cashier about a banana. Not the price, just the banana, which she said had been sold to her as organic. I felt a wave of tenderness for her so large that my knees went weak. I knew the exact number of her hairs. I knew she had cried in her car that morning and not told anyone why.

The eggs slipped out of my hand. Twelve of them broke on the linoleum.

"Sir?" said the cashier. "Are you okay?"

"I made you," I said. It came out kinder than I meant, and much more frightening.

She took a step back. The banana woman stared at me. A teenager at the next register put his hand on his phone, and I understood that in about ten seconds there would be a video.

So here is what I learned in those ten seconds, and the reason I did what I did next. Being God is not like being a king. A king gets to decide. What I felt was every single thing at once: the cashier's sore feet, the banana woman's grief, the egg yolk spreading into the grout, a child dying in a city I could not pronounce, and another being born in it that same minute. I felt it all and I was holding all of it, and I was not able to put any of it down.

I had forgotten once already. I knew that now. The knowledge came with a feeling like the end of a long vacation, the feeling of having left something unbearable behind on purpose. I had made a world full of creatures who could not be certain of anything, and then I had stepped inside to be one of them, because it was the only way to be gentle with them. Watching from above was too much. Living among them, you could at least be tired. You could at least buy detergent.

"Sorry," I said to the cashier. "I'll pay for the eggs."

"Don't worry about it," she said, still wary. "Maybe go sit down."

I did. I sat on the bench by the shopping carts, in the loud afternoon light, and I made the decision. It was not dramatic. There was no thunder. I simply let go of the knowing, the way you let go of a breath. I thought about forgetting as hard as I could. I thought about my mother's kitchen, my overdue library book, my knee that ached before rain.

It worked quickly. The oranges were only oranges again. The sky was only the sky, a thing that happened to me.

A man sat down beside me and asked if I was all right. I said I thought I had stood up too fast.

"Happens to me too," he said. We watched the parking lot together.

I will say this, though. For a moment after, something small stayed behind, like a coin in a coat pocket. When the banana woman came out and dropped her keys, I picked them up, and neither of us knew why my hands were so careful.

text:
Working from Home: Benefits and Drawbacks

In recent years, working from home has become common in many countries. Improvements in technology and changes brought by the pandemic have allowed millions of people to do their jobs without going to an office. This shift has clear advantages, but it also brings real disadvantages.

The most obvious benefit is flexibility. Employees save the time and money they would otherwise spend commuting, and many use those hours to sleep, exercise, or be with family. Remote workers can often arrange their schedules around personal needs, which can improve both happiness and productivity. Employers also gain, since they may spend less on office space and can hire talented people from anywhere rather than only from nearby. In addition, fewer commuters means less traffic and lower carbon emissions, which is good for the environment.

However, working from home is not without problems. One major issue is isolation. Without daily contact with coworkers, people can feel lonely and disconnected, and casual conversations that spark ideas or build friendships tend to disappear. Another difficulty is separating work from private life. When the kitchen table is also the desk, some people end up working longer hours and find it hard to switch off. Distractions at home, such as noise, family members, or household chores, can also reduce concentration. Furthermore, workers who are not visible in the office may feel overlooked when promotions are decided, and younger employees can miss out on learning from more experienced colleagues.

In conclusion, working from home offers freedom, savings, and environmental benefits, but it can harm social connection, work-life balance, and career development. For most people, a hybrid arrangement, combining a few days at home with a few days in the office, may offer the best balance. Whatever the choice, companies and workers should be honest about what actually works for them.

# Rosberg Quickest in Australian Grand Prix Practice as Vettel Impresses on Ferrari Debut

MELBOURNE — Nico Rosberg set the pace in practice for the Australian Grand Prix on Friday, finishing ahead of Mercedes teammate Lewis Hamilton as the new Formula One season got under way.

Rosberg posted the fastest lap of the session, with Hamilton close behind in second. The two dominated last season, when Mercedes won all but three of the 19 races, and the early signs suggest the team will again be the car to beat at Albert Park. Rivals will have noted that the Silver Arrows looked comfortable and quick on a track where reliability and pace both matter.

Sebastian Vettel, driving for Ferrari for the first time, made a promising start with his new team. The four-time world champion finished third in the second practice session, an encouraging result for a team that has struggled to challenge Mercedes. Vettel's move from Red Bull was one of the major stories of the winter, and fans and rivals alike were watching to see how quickly he would adapt to the Italian team's car.

Away from the track, the weekend has been overshadowed by a legal dispute involving Sauber. Giedo van der Garde does not race for the team in Melbourne despite a court ruling in his favor. The Dutch driver had gone to court over his contract with the Swiss team, and the ruling had raised expectations that he would take part. Instead, the situation remained unresolved, and he was not in the car as practice began. The episode has added an unwelcome distraction for a team that already faces financial pressure.

For now, the focus will return to qualifying, where Mercedes will aim to lock out the front row once again. Ferrari hopes Vettel's pace is not a one-off, and that the team has made enough progress over the winter to close the gap. The race is scheduled for Sunday.

**Abstract**

Building population-level templates of the central nervous system is essential for studying anatomical variability and for enabling consistent analysis across subjects. Existing atlases typically cover either the brain or the spinal cord, and they rarely account for the continuous anatomy that links the two. We present a generative framework for constructing diffeomorphic atlases from combined brain and spinal cord magnetic resonance imaging data. The method estimates a mean template and a distribution of smooth, invertible deformations that map the template to individual subjects, preserving topology and permitting statistical analysis of shape. We address the large differences in field of view and anatomical curvature between brain and cervical cord by using a multi-scale registration scheme with region-specific regularization. The model is trained on a heterogeneous dataset of healthy volunteers and evaluated on held-out scans. Results show improved alignment accuracy and sharper template structure compared with existing atlas construction methods, and the learned deformation model captures plausible anatomical variation. The resulting atlas offers a foundation for studying neurological disease along the entire neuraxis.

text:
The Fourth Window

Boy, it's a joyous day outside!

That was what Mr. Albrecht said every morning for forty-one years, and every morning the nurses at Linden Court smiled and said yes, it certainly was. He said it at the window of room 12, and he said it in a voice that filled the hallway like warm bread.

Today he said it to nobody.

Nora, the new aide, stood in the doorway holding a tray of oatmeal and watched his back. The window was open a few inches. Through it came the sounds of a spring morning: a lawnmower, a screen door, children on a sidewalk somewhere deciding who was it. A cardinal sat on the dogwood and sang as if nothing had ever gone wrong in the world.

"Boy," he said again, quieter. "It's a joyous day outside."

She had been told about him. The other aides said he used to run the hardware store on Fifth, that his wife, Ruth, had died in March, and that they had always taken their coffee at this window, two chairs, one small table. Now there was one chair. The second had been moved to the corner, and nobody had asked him to move it.

"Would you like your breakfast, Mr. Albrecht?"

"Ruth always said you could tell a good day by the noise," he said. "She liked to count the sounds. Seven was a fair morning. Ten was a joyous one."

Nora set down the tray. "How many today?"

He was quiet for a long time. The lawnmower coughed and stopped.

"Eleven," he said. "I counted eleven before you came in."

She waited.

"It's the most I've ever heard," he said. "And she's not here to hear it."

The cardinal flew from the dogwood. A car passed, and its radio played something with a trumpet in it. Down on the sidewalk, a girl in a yellow raincoat, though there was no rain, was dragging a stick along the fence, and the fence rattled like a drum that nobody wanted to play.

Nora had not known what to say to the dying, or to the people left behind by them. She had been trained in blood pressure and transfers, not in this. So she did the only thing that occurred to her. She pulled the chair out of the corner and set it beside his.

"Tell me what you hear," she said.

He turned and looked at her for the first time. His eyes were wet, and he did not seem ashamed of it. "The lawnmower," he said. "That's one. The screen door."

"Two."

"The children. That's a lot of them. Say three."

"Three," she agreed.

They counted together. A dog, a sprinkler, a bus changing gears at the corner. Each sound had been a small gift to Ruth, he said, and now it was a small weight that he had to carry in her place. All that noise, all that life, and the one person he wanted to share it with had stopped hearing it.

When they reached twelve, he laughed, a short and cracked sound, then covered his mouth as if the laugh had been rude.

"Boy," he whispered, "it's a joyous day outside."

"It is," Nora said. "I'm sorry."

He nodded and looked out at the bright, loud morning that went on without Ruth. Then he reached over and, very gently, rested his hand on the arm of the empty chair.

text: The claim "four out of five dentists recommend" is a marketing statement, and its meaning depends on how the underlying survey was conducted. Companies do sometimes survey dentists, but the sample is often small, and the question is frequently phrased loosely. Respondents may be asked whether they would recommend a product, or they may be allowed to name several brands, which means that many brands can each claim to be endorsed by most dentists. The figure therefore does not necessarily indicate that 80 percent of dentists prefer that toothpaste above all others. Consumers should look for the sample size, the exact wording of the question, and evidence of independent approval, such as the seal of a recognized dental association.

I do recommend Dr. Mercy, with some qualifications, and the nationality or language of your teammates should not be the deciding factor. Whether a hero suits you depends on the composition of the team, your playstyle, and the match-up, not on where your teammates come from.

**The case for Mercy.** Angela Ziegler is one of the most effective support heroes in Overwatch. Her healing beam provides steady sustain, her damage boost increases the output of strong damage dealers, and her ability to resurrect a fallen ally can turn a team fight. Because she is highly mobile, she can stay close to allies while avoiding enemy fire. Mercy is also relatively accessible, and many players find her easy to learn at the start.

**Communication.** If you are playing alongside Chinese teammates, a language barrier may complicate coordination. Mercy is a good choice here for a practical reason: her role requires less verbal communication than many others. A Mercy player can follow the flow of the fight by watching health bars and positioning, and can contribute without extended discussion. Learning a few basic phrases in Chinese, such as terms for healing, ultimate readiness, and retreating, can help. The in-game ping system is also universal and should be used often. Voice lines and text callouts for ultimates can be understood by players regardless of their language.

**Limitations.** Mercy does have drawbacks. She is vulnerable to enemy snipers and flankers, and she has little offensive capability. If your team is facing heavy dive compositions, you may need to choose a hero with more self-defense, such as Lucio, Brigitte, or Ana. Mercy also depends on her teammates making good use of her support, so a disorganized team can limit her value.

**Practical advice.**
- Prioritize your own positioning, staying near cover and close to a front-line ally.
- Alternate between healing and damage boost according to what the situation requires.
- Save resurrection for moments when it can restore a decisive advantage, rather than using it reflexively.
- Be prepared to switch if the team is struggling, and treat your teammates with courtesy regardless of language.

In summary, Mercy is a sound and often valuable choice for supporting any team, including one composed of Chinese players. Success depends more on your skill, awareness, and willingness to adapt than on the language of your teammates.

# Boko Haram Reportedly Pledges Allegiance to ISIS

Nigerian militant group Boko Haram has reportedly pledged its allegiance to ISIS, a move that could link two of the world's most feared extremist organizations, though experts say the immediate effect on the ground may be limited.

The reported pledge would mark a significant step for Boko Haram, which has carried out bombings, kidnappings and mass killings in northeastern Nigeria and neighboring countries for years. The group is best known internationally for the abduction of hundreds of schoolgirls from the town of Chibok. By aligning itself with ISIS, which controls territory in Syria and Iraq, Boko Haram appears to be seeking greater prominence within the global jihadist movement.

Analysts note that such declarations often carry as much symbolic weight as operational meaning. Peter Pham, an expert on African security issues, said the merger is unlikely to alter the military situation in the short term.

"In the short term, the merger won't have a big impact on the battlefield," Pham said, suggesting that the practical challenges of coordinating across thousands of miles will limit any immediate effect. Boko Haram and ISIS operate in very different environments, and neither group is believed to be in a position to send large numbers of fighters or substantial resources to the other quickly.

Even so, observers say the pledge could have longer-term consequences. An association with ISIS may help Boko Haram with recruitment and propaganda, and it could open the door to more sharing of tactics, training and funding over time. It may also encourage regional governments and international partners to treat the threat as part of a broader fight against ISIS.

The Nigerian government and its neighbors have been working to push back against Boko Haram, but the group has continued to carry out deadly attacks. Officials have not yet commented in detail on the reported pledge, and it is not clear how ISIS will respond to the declaration.

text: **Abstract.** Quantifying model uncertainty is a central problem in the statistical analysis of complex systems, particularly when observed data depart from Gaussian assumptions. Conventional approaches typically rely on Gaussian approximations or on measures that are sensitive to heavy tails and skewness. In this work, we propose a framework that uses the Hellinger distance to assess the discrepancy between candidate models and the distribution of non-Gaussian observations. Because the Hellinger distance is bounded and symmetric, it offers stable comparisons across models with differing supports and tail behavior. We derive estimators for the distance based on observed data, establish their consistency under mild conditions, and describe how the resulting values may be used to rank models and to construct uncertainty bounds. Numerical experiments on synthetic and real datasets demonstrate that the proposed method detects model misspecification more reliably than comparable Gaussian-based measures. The results indicate that the Hellinger distance provides a robust and interpretable tool for uncertainty quantification in non-Gaussian settings.

text:
The Doctor of Villains

Dr. Miriam Castellan's practice occupied the thirteenth floor of a building that did not appear on any map, which her clients appreciated. Her waiting room was kept deliberately plain: three chairs, a ficus, and a small sign requesting that capes be left at the door.

Her first appointment of the day was a man who called himself the Orchid. He arrived exactly on time, as he always did, and took the chair nearest the window. He disliked sitting with his back to a door.

"Good morning, Doctor," he said. "I have been thinking about our last session."

"I am glad to hear it. What came up for you?"

"You asked me why I wished to flood the harbor district." He straightened a cuff. "I answered that it was a matter of principle. On reflection, I do not believe that was a complete answer."

Miriam made a short note. In eleven years of practice she had learned that the most important progress came in these small, hesitant admissions, spoken in a tone of dry formality. "What do you think the complete answer might be?"

"My father owned a small warehouse near the water. It was lost when the city rebuilt the docks. No one asked him. No one apologized." He paused. "I told myself that I was correcting an injustice on behalf of thousands. I am no longer certain it was thousands. I suspect it may have been one."

"That is a significant observation."

"It is also an inconvenient one. I have already purchased the dam."

She allowed herself a small smile, which she kept professional. "We can discuss the dam. But first, how did it feel to say that aloud?"

The Orchid considered the question for some time. "Lighter," he said. "Which is not what I expected."

Her work, as she often explained to colleagues at conferences who could not be told the full details, did not involve convincing anyone that they were wrong. Her clients were intelligent, driven, and frequently correct about the flaws of the world. Her task was narrower. She helped them separate the grievance from the plan, the wound from the weapon. A villain, in her experience, was rarely a person without a conscience. More often he was a person with a conscience that had been left alone for too long.

Her second client, later that afternoon, was a woman who preferred to be addressed as Madame Frost. She did not sit. She walked the length of the office twice before speaking, and Miriam let her.

"I am told I have anger issues," Madame Frost said at last.

"Who told you?"

"My lieutenants. They left a pamphlet on my desk. It was laminated."

"That was thoughtful of them, if not tactful."

"I froze the pamphlet." Madame Frost stopped at the window. "I would like you to know that I regret it. It was a very well-made pamphlet."

"Then we have something to begin with."

By evening, Miriam was tired in the way she always was, with the heavy tiredness that came from listening carefully to people who rarely were listened to at all. She filed her notes in the locked cabinet, watered the ficus, and turned off the lights.

At the door she paused, as she did every night. Colleagues sometimes asked whether she was afraid. She was, occasionally. But she had come to believe that the most dangerous people were the ones nobody was willing to sit across from, and that the bravest thing she could offer any of them was an hour of ordinary attention.

She locked the door and went home.
